features.description: Add an optional user_impact object to the feature contract in agent-conventions with conditional semantics on audience, plus a description_hash binding the declaration to the text it was written against
steps: Add user_impact to features.schema.json: audience (enum end_user, operator, agent, none), summary (string), surfaces (reuse the plan-level surfaces enum), and description_hash (string)

Conditional semantics per D003: when audience is 'none', summary and surfaces MUST be absent or empty — a one-word declaration is the whole answer; when audience is any other value, summary (>=10 chars) and non-empty surfaces are required. Express as a JSON Schema if/then/else so both the JSON and Pydantic paths agree
description_hash is a digest of the feature description at the moment user_impact was authored — this is the staleness anchor, replacing the timestamp approach D005 originally proposed
Bump agent-conventions VERSION and commit in that repo
Subtree-pull the new version into DontPanic claude/shared/ and re-run validate.py over every existing DontPanic plan to prove the addition is backward-compatible
features.acceptance: validate.py passes on all existing DontPanic plans with no user_impact present (proving optionality); accepts audience:none carrying neither summary nor surfaces; rejects audience:none that also carries a summary; rejects audience:end_user missing summary, with a summary under 10 chars, or with empty surfaces; and accepts a well-formed end_user declaration including description_hash.

features.description: Metadata delivery — snapshot a typed DecisionBrief onto NotifyEvent at pause-emission time, because the live dispatcher calls render(event) with no plan_meta or feature_meta and would otherwise always report impact undeclared
steps: Confirm the gap first: event_copy.render(event, plan_meta=None, feature_meta=None) is how notify_event.py invokes it — the optional metadata parameters are never supplied on the production path, so any feature reading them alone is dead code in practice
Define a frozen DecisionBrief dataclass carrying what_changes, user_impact, affected_audience, decision_consequence, reversible, and impact_status (declared, undeclared, possibly_stale)
Build the brief at the supervisor's pause-emission site where plan and feature data are in scope, and attach it to NotifyEvent as an immutable snapshot
One snapshot serves every sink — INBOX, notify, dashboard, and the CLI prompt all read the same frozen object rather than each re-deriving from plan artifacts at different times
Compute impact_status at snapshot time: possibly_stale when the feature description's current digest differs from user_impact.description_hash (D005)
features.acceptance: pytest tests/test_decision_brief_delivery.py passes: a pause emitted through the real supervisor path produces a NotifyEvent carrying a populated DecisionBrief without any caller passing plan_meta or feature_meta; the brief is frozen and identical across all four sinks for one event; impact_status is 'declared' for a matching description_hash, 'possibly_stale' for a mismatched one, and 'undeclared' when user_impact is absent.

features.description: Widen the copy contract with four distinct fields — what_changes, user_impact, affected_audience, decision_consequence — keeping plain_consequence's existing meaning intact rather than repurposing it
steps: Add what_changes, user_impact, and affected_audience to _Template and RenderedEvent, all defaulting to None so existing table rows keep compiling
Preserve plain_consequence for its documented meaning — 'what happens if I do this' — and populate it from DecisionBrief.decision_consequence, NOT from product impact

Correct the current aliasing: operator_console.py:1314 sets plain_consequence to rendered.detail, which fills the plain-language slot with orchestration prose. Replace that with the real decision consequence
Stop hardcoding reversible=False at operator_console.py:1314 for event-derived items; carry DecisionBrief.reversible through instead
Leave technical_metadata untouched — orchestration detail keeps its existing home
features.acceptance: pytest tests/test_event_copy_brief_fields.py passes: RenderedEvent carries all four new fields; plain_consequence on an event-derived ActionItem equals the brief's decision_consequence and is never equal to rendered.detail; reversible reflects the brief rather than a hardcoded False; a regression test asserts the pre-change aliasing does not return.

features.description: Rewrite the renderable approval-class templates impact-first — product outcome leads, orchestration identifiers demote to a supporting reference line
steps: Enumerate the renderable needs_action kinds — those whose disposition is LIVE or DASHBOARD_ACTION. INBOX_ONLY and AUDIT_ONLY kinds (error among them) never reach render() and are explicitly out of this feature's surface
Rewrite each renderable headline to lead with what changes and who feels it, falling back to the current copy shape when impact is undeclared
Move plan_label, gate, and stage to a supporting reference line per USER.md:15
Keep exact_command and the D008 honest-commands rule unchanged — this feature changes prose only
Preserve every fact the old copy carried; demotion means relocated, never dropped
features.acceptance: pytest tests/test_event_copy_impact_first.py passes: (a) all 27 INBOX kinds still resolve to exactly one disposition and the existing totality test is green; (b) every kind that rendered before still renders; (c) every renderable needs_action variant receives a brief; (d) events with no feature in scope, and plan-level events, get a distinct honest fallback rather than a feature-shaped one; (e) rendered headlines for renderable needs_action kinds contain the impact summary and do not lead with the plan id; (f) a field-level diff proves no previously-present fact is absent and exact_command values are byte-identical.

features.description: Undeclared and stale impact honesty rules plus a non-blocking plan-lock advisory — the renderer states what it does not know and never synthesizes a claim
steps: When impact_status is undeclared, render the literal fallback 'User impact not declared for this feature.' and no substitute prose
When impact_status is possibly_stale, render the declared summary explicitly marked as written against an earlier version of this feature — never present it as current
Add a source-level test asserting no approval template body is ever populated from model output at render time (D002)
Add an advisory lint at the plan lock path naming features whose plan declares ux, ios, web, or android surfaces but that carry no user_impact
The lint prints and exits 0 — it never refuses the lock (D004) — and includes the exact fix (edit features.json)
features.acceptance: pytest tests/test_event_copy_undeclared_impact.py passes: a gate on a feature with no user_impact renders the exact fallback string with no synthesized prose; a stale declaration renders marked as stale rather than current; the non-generative source assertion holds; `dontpanic plan lock` on a ux-surfaced fixture missing user_impact prints an advisory naming each feature and exits 0; the same plan with user_impact declared prints no advisory.

features.description: Approval-surface parity — CLI approve, INBOX, notify (Discord + terminal), and the dashboard card all render the same brief from the single F002 snapshot
steps: Thread the brief through the CLI approve/resume prompt so the operator sees it while deciding, not only in the notification that summoned them
Wire it into inbox.py, notify.py, notify_discord.py, and the dashboard ActionItem card, all reading the frozen DecisionBrief
Apply per-surface truncation from D006 — Discord and terminal-notifier abbreviate, the dashboard renders unabridged
Truncation preserves the impact line and shortens supporting detail, never the reverse
Confirm existing secret scrubbing runs over the new fields at every emit point
features.acceptance: pytest tests/test_brief_surface_parity.py passes: one synthetic gate rendered through all four surfaces yields identical what_changes / user_impact / affected_audience / decision_consequence values modulo declared truncation; a summary exceeding the Discord cap keeps the impact line and truncates supporting detail; _assert_no_secret_shapes passes over each surface's payload with a token-shaped string planted in user_impact.summary.

features.description: Worked example on an in-repo fixture plus authoring guidance for writing a useful user_impact
steps: Build the worked example as a DontPanic-owned fixture plan under tests/fixtures/, seeded from the shape of the Glam sticky-first gate with provenance recorded in the fixture header — this plan's Target is DontPanic and agent-conventions, and authoring into a third repo is outside its authority
Capture the fixture gate rendered under the old templates and under the new ones, side by side in evidence/
Write authoring guidance covering the four audience values, what separates a useful summary from a restated description, and worked examples of each
Add the guidance to the plan-artifacts skill so it reaches authors at plan-writing time
Record in USER.md that the builder-facing preference now has enforcement behind it, linking this plan
features.acceptance: evidence/ contains before.txt and after.txt for the in-repo fixture gate showing both renders, and the fixture header records what it was modelled on; the authoring guidance exists and is referenced from the plan-artifacts skill; a reviewer reading only after.txt can state what changes, who feels it, and what approving does without opening plan.md; no file outside DontPanic and agent-conventions is modified by this plan.
